title: Cost per accepted artifact
summary: Account for all attempts and remaining human work, with estimates labeled.

sections.label: Defined comparison
sections.text:
For one workload and reporting window:
cost per accepted artifact =
(model + tools/connectors + runner + validation + review/repair cost across ALL attempts)
/ accepted artifacts
With zero accepted artifacts, report no accepted outcome; do not divide by zero.

sections.label: Denominator
sections.text: Acceptance means meeting agreed usability criteria. Count the accepted task/artifact once; repairs are not extra successes. Include failed/rejected attempts in cost. Separate first-pass and repaired acceptance.

sections.label: Evidence labels
rows: Future demand, bursts and task mix

sections.label: Explicit units
sections.text: Keep engineer minutes separate unless an agreed cost conversion exists. Separate build effort, recurring maintenance and per-run cost; avoid double-counting.

sections.label: Runtime/billing evidence
sections.text: An IDE subscription alone does not establish backend access. Verify organization enablement, billing owner and task/report correlation. GitHub documents the SDK usage cost field as a request multiplier rather than currency.

sections.label: Forecast
sections.text: Use volume assumptions and ranges that show what changes the recommendation. Measurements and estimates can coexist. A cheaper model helps only when total accepted-outcome evidence supports it.

basis: Ticket-scoped recommendation; not an implemented workplace capability
confidence: Moderate for fit; workplace benefit unknown

catalog.applicability: Illustrative context. Compare its assumptions with your own work.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
